summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for chest pressure, epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and constipation. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal EKGs and negative troponins. Abdominal imaging showed no obstruction but supported constipation as a contributor. Symptoms improved after a GI cocktail and bowel movements with laxatives. Her chest pain was attributed to GERD, and she was started on ranitidine. Acute kidney injury, likely prerenal from dehydration, improved with IV fluids. Her home medications were continued, with instructions to restart lisinopril and HCTZ. She expressed concern about unsafe housing due to cockroach infestation, prompting social work consultation. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for a stress test and medication management.
